title: Milky Way over Avenue of Baobabs
caption: The Milky Way over the Avenue of Baobabs, Morondava, Madagascar
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: The band of the Milky Way stretches across the sky above the Avenue of Baobabs in Morondava, Madagascar, in this photograph taken in 2017. The baobab trees stand in silhouette in the foreground.
Baobabs are unusual trees, with thick, barrel-like trunks, and they are known for living a very long time. Seen against the night sky, their distinctive shapes frame the view.

The Milky Way is our own galaxy. Because we live inside its flat disc, we see it from within as a soft band of light running across the sky, made of the combined glow of countless distant stars too faint to pick out one by one. Dark lanes often seen along the band are clouds of dust that block light from the stars behind them. The band shows up most clearly where the sky is dark, away from city lights.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera in visible light. The camera settings and processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed than it would to someone standing among the trees.
